messages:
raj: quick flag — after rolling kernel-selector v2 (commit 2b3c4d5) we've got a noticeable host-side perf delta. 99p tail up ~30-40ms and host CPU ~9-11% higher on a subset of machines. pprof points at http2_frame_read -> grpc_decode_headers -> pretokenize_scan -> kvcache.get -> many small writev syscalls.

raj: snippet from the flame:```
27.4%  http2_frame_read
20.9%  grpc_decode_headers
14.3%  pretokenize_scan
9.6%   kvcache.get
6.7%   writev (lots of <512B writes)
```

evan: thanks. quick question: did v2 change the minibatch/prefetch hints? small batches can amplify host parse cost. which traffic slice did this hit?

raj: mostly medium-short seq traffic (mobile API path). rollout was global but with gradual waves over 6h. pprof: https://internal/prof/6550012345/pprof.html

nicole: observing kv miss delta on the mobile path as well — pre-roll our miss% ~3.5%, post-roll ~8.7% on the same hostpool. raw counters: total lookups 2,400,000, misses 209k.

nicole: ```
kv_total: 2,400,000
kv_miss: 209,000 # 8.7%
kv_miss_prev: 84,000 # 3.5%
```

anita: hypothesis: kernel v2 picks a kernel layout/sequence alignment that shifts the kv key stride or increases differentially-packed meta keys; that causes more cacheline churn and extra proto_unwrap passes. also the frame assembler seems to flush smaller frames after tokenization -> more writev ops.

matt: agree with the theory. immediate mitigations we can try: (1) sidecar coalescer — merge small header+payload fragments into one buffer before parsing, (2) in-proxy writev aggregator (group small iovecs), (3) override kernel-selector to prefer previous kernel for mobile path traffic until fix.

kai: add to that: tune gRPC windowing for streaming endpoints — current window size seems to cause many small DATA frames when tokenization emits partial chunks. increasing write buffer threshold slightly can reduce syscall rate.

ev an: (edited) I'll put together PR to add a kernel-selector bias flag and a metric gate that auto-opts-back to previous kernel when per-worker small_write_rate > 300/s for 5m. Also will add a health-check label so infra can route mobile traffic off canary quickly.

anita: I'll prototype the sidecar coalescer in Rust as a thin transform: collect inbound bytes up to 4KB or 8ms, then forward single buffer. Feature-flagged and opt-in per-hostgroup. ben used similar for edge in the past and saw big write reductions.

nicole: I'll instrument kv key histogram to see if key distribution changed (prefix lengths, alignment). also adding per-request writev_count histogram to alert on regressions.

raj: rolling a traffic-split canary: 95% v2 : 5% previous on tag hostgroup=mobile-canary. early 20m telemetry: canary hosts with previous kernel show p99 latency -28ms and CPU -6% vs v2 hosts. writev count dropped ~70% on canary.

matt: good. owners? Evan for selector bias PR; Anita + Nicole pair for sidecar coalesce; Kai add microbench to perf-ci that runs header-decode + tokenization with a variety of fragment sizes and both kernels. I'll review PR B (selector gate) tonight.

anita: plan: will land coalescer behind ff, run canary (10 hosts) for 24h, collect cpu/writev/kv-miss deltas. if stable, roll to hostpool.

nicole: microbench idea: synthetic stream generator that emits header+payload in 64/128/256/512 byte fragments to measure parsing and writev cost across kernels. I'll add it to perf-ci and include kv-hit/miss counters.

raj: created tracking issue INF-2456 and assigned owners. SRE, can you create an incident for tracking?

sre-bot: created incident INC-2026-043 (host-ingress-parse-uplift) linked to INF-2456 and thread 6550012345

matt: one more ask — add a derived dashboard metric parse_token_pct that sums http2_frame_read + grpc_decode_headers + pretokenize_scan CPU on hosts. wire a paging alert if parse_token_pct increases >5% over baseline for 10m.

kai: will add bench and alert rules to perf-ci and dashboards. also recommend adding a unit test that asserts writev_count per-request < 8 for typical requests, to kill future regressions.

evan: I'll open PR with gated rollback and emergency re-route plan. ETA 2h for draft.

anita: coalescer draft ETA 3-4h, will keep minimal logic (time+size) and no parsing dependencies.

raj: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene in 2h with canary telemetry. post any quick logs or flame links here.
